newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - German rate woes push up Euromark vol.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - German rate woes push up Euromark vol.

text.p: Changing expectations of the likely course of German interest rates sparked a rally in implied volatility of Euromark options traded on LIFFE so far this week, traders said on Wednesday.
Recently, the weakness of the mark has raised speculation that a rise in German interest rates may come sooner than previoulsy thought.
"It's suddenly a very nervous market," said an options trader at a British bank. "There's potentially a lot further to go on the upside for the volatility."

Implied volatility of September Euromark options rose to 10.1/11.3 percent by 1000 GMT, up around 10 basis points on Tuesday, and on the back of a 50 basis point rise on Monday. December was up a similar amount at 12.3/13.00 and March rose to 13.55/14.5 percent.

The German repo rate currently stands at 3.00 percent, and has not moved since August 1996. The Lombard and Discount rates of 4.5 and 2.5 have been unmoved since April 1996. Germany last raised rates in mid-1992.
"Volatility was getting too low, and now a lot of people are afraid," said a trader at a French market maker on LIFFE. "I can seen September getting to 17 percent."
Euromark volatility had been on a downward path since the beginning of the year when it was around 16.0 percent.
Traders said volume in Euromark options was calmer this session, with put buying dominating trade.
"Yesterday people sold straddles and puts, and I'd expect to see them buying them back," said the French market-maker.
December Euromarks were quoted at 96.64, up two basis points on the day and well off a recent peak of 96.79 on July 8.
